title: The mountain again (Mark 9:1–13)
hook: the transfiguration, then down the mountain into need

segments.voice: Yesterday, who do you say I am: Peter got the answer right and the meaning wrong. Your line was take up your cross. What did you carry quietly? Six days later, a mountain. Day two hundred fifteen.

Some moments you want to bottle. A wedding night. A retreat. A concert where everyone sang the last chorus together. You don't want to go home. Today three fishermen get the biggest moment of their lives. Six days after the hard talk about the cross, Jesus takes Peter, James and John and leads them up a high mountain, alone. In Mark, mountains are where things happen: he went up one to pray, and up one to call the twelve. This time something happens to him. And then, as always, they have to walk back down.
screen: `MOMENTS YOU WANT TO BOTTLE.` → `THREE FRIENDS, A HIGH MOUNTAIN.` → `THEN, THE WALK BACK DOWN.`

segments.voice: First, the change. Mark says he was transfigured before them, and his clothes became shining white, whiter than any cloth-bleacher on earth could make them. That's Mark's voice: a fisherman's-eye detail about laundry, next to the glory of God. The Greek word is where we get metamorphosis. Second, the company. Elijah and Moses appear, talking with Jesus. Moses gave the Law. Elijah stood for the prophets. The whole story of Israel, standing on one mountaintop with him. Third, Peter. He blurts out, in the Douay-Rheims: "Rabbi, it is good for us to be here: and let us make three tabernacles." Tents. Stay here. Keep it. Mark adds, kindly, that Peter didn't know what to say, because they were terrified. Then a cloud covers them, and a voice: "This is my most beloved son; hear ye him." Hear him. The Father doesn't say build him a tent. He says listen. And suddenly, looking around, they see no one anymore but Jesus only. Fourth, the way down. On the path Jesus tells them not to tell anyone until the Son of man has risen from the dead, and they argue about what rising from the dead could even mean. They ask about Elijah, and he says Elijah has already come, meaning John the Baptist. Nobody gets to stay on the mountain. The glory isn't a place to live. It's something to carry down. And at the bottom, tomorrow, a crowd and a desperate father are already waiting.
screen: `TRANSFIGURED: WHITER THAN BLEACH.` · `MOSES AND ELIJAH WITH HIM.` · `LET US BUILD THREE TENTS.` · `NOBODY STAYS ON THE MOUNTAIN.` · then, large: `THIS IS MY MOST BELOVED SON; HEAR YE HIM.`

segments.voice: Here's the practice: go from prayer to service. For the first minute, just sit. Breathe. If you pray, rest in whatever prayer you have, or in the words hear ye him. If you don't, let yourself enjoy the quiet, like a view from a high place. Then, for the second minute, walk down the mountain in your mind. Who's at the bottom today? Someone who needs a call, a ride, a meal, an apology. Pick one person. Decide one thing you'll do. The bell holds the time.
The mountain again. The transfiguration: three friends see Jesus shining, hear the voice say hear him, and then walk back down. Today's word.
Your line: down the mountain. Today, after any good moment, prayer or otherwise, carry it straight to the one thing you decided to do. Day two hundred fifteen.

howItsDone: Catholics celebrate the Feast of the Transfiguration on August 6, and the story is read every year on the Second Sunday of Lent, as a glimpse of glory before the road to the cross.

fork.setup: you're Peter on the mountain. Jesus is shining, Moses and Elijah are there, and you're terrified. what do you say?

let's go and tell everyone right now.
fork.reveal: "Rabbi, it is good for us to be here: and let us make three tabernacles." Mark says he didn't know what to say. then the cloud, and the voice: hear him.

original.note: Greek: he was transfigured, from the same root as metamorphosis.

trapdoor: what you thought: a glowing Jesus on a hill.
what it means: the Law and the Prophets beside him, a voice saying hear him, and then the walk back down to people in need.
what a scholar hears: metemorphōthē, 'he was transformed'; the Vulgate and Douay number the verses one lower here than most English Bibles.

notes: Douay-Rheims Mark 9:4 and 9:6 given from memory; confirm wording. In the Vulgate/Douay, the 'some standing here' verse is 8:39, so chapter 9 runs one lower than KJV numbering; the outline's 'Mark 9:1–13' follows the common numbering. Confirm references.
The clothes detail (Mark 9:2 DR / 9:3 KJV, 'no fuller upon earth') is paraphrased as 'cloth-bleacher'; confirm.
Moses and Elijah as the Law and the Prophets is a traditional reading; confirm framing.
Transfiguration feast on August 6 and the Gospel on the Second Sunday of Lent (all three years, from the synoptic in turn): confirm.
